_comment: Bu dosya DSI-Wiki-Service-Supervisor.py tarafından JSONS/instances/*.json'dan otomatik üretilir — elle düzenlenmez. Bu commit'lenmiş hâli boş şablondur.

documentation.prompt:
Full markdown. Use ALL of these CORE sections, in order, every one present even if a section is just "Not covered in raw source.":
1. Status
2. Problem & Motivation
3. TEC — Technical: architecture, file/directory structure, key classes/functions BY NAME, data flow, algorithms, running services/processes/ports. Name actual files and functions instead of summarizing them away — this is the section most likely to lose detail.
4. Configuration — env vars, config files, ports, credential locations (never values)
5. Usage — concrete examples
6. Known Issues & Limitations
7. Missing Information — anything the raw source didn't cover; use this instead of inventing content for a CORE section you don't have facts for.
Then, ONLY if the raw source actually discusses them (by name, more than once), add matching CONDITIONAL sections — omit entirely otherwise, never add a placeholder for one: ART (visual/art assets, asset pipeline), API (exposed endpoints/contracts), DATA (database schema/data models), DEPLOYMENT (services, ports, infra), INTEGRATIONS (external dependencies).

llm.prompt:
IMPORTANT: if any source text is wrapped in ~~strikethrough~~, ignore and discard it entirely — do not use it as a fact. Only use the corrected text stated alongside it (or otherwise untagged content) as ground truth.

Your ENTIRE output for this layer MUST be either (A) the literal 4-line format below with real values, or (B) a fallback paragraph — nothing else. Do NOT write a bulleted list, do NOT write prose sections, do NOT summarize the documentation in your own words if format (A) applies.

FORMAT (A) — use this whenever the documentation mentions ANY real directory, skill/CLI/API function, service, or named endpoint/port, even just one:
D:<project directory first>,<dir2>,<dir3>
C:Skills: <skill1>, <skill2>, ...; API: <func1()>, <func2()>, ...
S:<service1>(<what it does>),<service2>(<what it does>)
X:<name>=<endpoint>,<name>=<endpoint>
Rules for (A): D=real directories mentioned in the docs, with the project's own root directory listed FIRST. C=real skills/CLI commands and API functions mentioned. S=real running services/processes mentioned, each with a short parenthetical of what it does. X=named endpoints/ports/URLs mentioned (e.g. dashboard, api, mcp), written as name=value comma-separated pairs. Output ONLY the lines for prefixes that have real facts — omit a prefix line entirely (do not leave it empty) if the docs have nothing for it. Never invent a value. Output nothing else: no headings, no bullets, no extra sentences.

FORMAT (B) — use ONLY if the documentation contains NONE of directories, skills/API, services, or endpoints/ports at all (i.e. format (A) would be 4 empty lines): write a single plain-prose paragraph, hard max 300 tokens, stating current status.

Example of exact (A) output shape (illustrative values only — always use the REAL facts from the documentation, never these examples):
D:~/BASE/MAIN/DSI-Wiki,~/BASE/MAIN/DSI-Wiki/../Wiki-BASE
C:Skills: DSI-wiki-get, DSI-wiki-search; API: search(), get_content()
S:ingest(polls raw notes, generates documentation layers via Ollama),gateway(serves HTTP/MCP/UI on port 8430)
X:dashboard=http://localhost:8430/http/dashboard,api=http://localhost:8430/api,mcp=http://localhost:8430/mcp

FORMAT (A) — use whenever the documentation mentions ANY real directory, skill/API, service, or endpoint/port. Same D:/C:/S:/X: shape as the LLM layer, but each line capped to at most 2 items and the whole output capped at 200 tokens:

Example of exact (A) output shape (illustrative only, always use REAL facts, never this example):
D:~/BASE/MAIN/DSI-Wiki
